messages:
Clara Nguyen: FYI noticed a sustained spike from EU tenants — primary model `redwood-gpt-large` hit concurrent slot limit in eu-west around 09:04 UTC. Some requests returned 503s then got rerouted to a much slower fallback, causing latency SLO violations. :grimacing:
Ryan Patel: ugh. Which fallback was in the chain? compatible-small or the generic CPU fallback?
Clara Nguyen: Started with compatible-small (quantized) but after that we hit that pool too so it spilled to cpu-generic, which is ~5-6x slower for p50.
Jess Morales: Do we have telemetry showing per-tenant spill counts? We should avoid noisy tenants triggering global slowdowns.
Maya Li: We have per-variant spill metrics but not exposed in console per-tenant. Could add "spill_count" and "spill_latency_p50/p95" dimensions.
Arjun Singh: Short-term: can we route premium-tenants to reserved capacity to avoid them getting spilled? Long-term: prefer graceful preferring compatible variants in-region before region-crossing.
Ryan Patel: Agree. Two questions: 1) routing precedence by tier (premium > standard > free) and 2) region affinity before variant downgrade. We need deterministic ordering.
Clara Nguyen: Proposal: when primary is saturated, run this sequence: 1) try in-region compatible-variant (same tier) 2) if saturated, try in-region lower-cost compatible (respecting tenant min_quality) 3) if still saturated, try cross-region compatible within same tier 4) finally, fallback to generic CPU (as last resort). Also add opt-out header for tenants who want strict version pinning.
Maya Li: Sounds good. UX-wise in Console we should show a small badge on model route: "Auto-escape enabled" and a tooltip with recent escapes + counts. Also expose per-tenant spill telemetry in tenant detail page.
Jess Morales: Implementation notes: router needs to consider (a) tenant tier, (b) tenant pinned variants, (c) region affinity, (d) variant capacity signals. We should add a fast-path cache for routing decisions for identical request signatures to avoid extra latency.
Arjun Singh: For signals, propose we use `variant_available_slots` + `slot_utilization_rate` + a short-term failure counter. If available_slots <= threshold, mark variant as saturated for Xs and avoid routing to it.
Clara Nguyen: Sample routing config (proto-ish):
```
route_policy: {
  precedence: ["tenant_tier", "region_affinity", "variant_compatibility"],
  saturation_threshold: 0.95,
  hold_window_secs: 45,
  fallback_order: ["in_region_compatible", "cross_region_compatible", "cpu_generic"],
  respect_pinned: true
}
```
Ryan Patel: We should gate the change behind a feature flag `auto_variant_escape_v2` and roll to 10% then 50% with canary tenants. deploy-bot: feature flag `auto_variant_escape_v2` created and staged in prod.
Maya Li: Telemetry to capture: `escape_attempts`, `escape_success_rate`, `latency_delta_ms` (primary vs served), `tenants_impacted`. Also add a dashboard tile for escapes by region and by tier.
Jess Morales: Edge case: tenant pinned to an exact model version — we must surface a clear error and/or honor pinning if tenant opted-in. Otherwise, default allow escapes.
Clara Nguyen: Action items: 1) Ryan/Jess to prototype router changes + cache (PR by EOD Wed) 2) Maya to mock Console badge + tenant spill table (mock by Thu) 3) Arjun to add saturation signals to telemetry and alert rule thresholds (threshold proposal PR) 4) I'll coordinate rollout and canary list.
Ryan Patel: I'll add a small unit test matrix for tier/region/variant combos. Will add e2e that simulates slot exhaustion.
Arjun Singh: I'll add an alert: if cross-region escapes > 10% for > 5m, page on-call.
Clara Nguyen: Thanks all. If we can get the PRs early next week we can ship gradual rollout before next traffic event. :thumbsup:
